A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DynamicID work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original single-ID and multi-ID generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, component ablations, parameter sensitivity results, and generated-image examples.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and reports additional quantitative and qualitative multi-ID baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The SAA operations, IMR architecture, training objectives, and two-stage training procedure remain unchanged. The revised abstract and additional SAA diagram clarify the existing method without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Training retains Laion-Face, VariFace-10k, and KDEF; evaluation retains CelebA and the same personalization tasks and prompt categories. The appendix applications are preserved. Additional comparators and fewer displayed single-ID examples do not change this coverage.

E2.justification: The multi-ID comparison adds OMG-InstantID and StoryMaker in Table 2 and Figure 6, alongside the retained FastComposer, Face-Diffuser, and UniPortrait. The single-ID comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 2 extends the multi-ID comparison to SDXL-based comparator configurations; v1 included only SD1.5-based methods there. Existing training settings, sampling procedure, metrics, 500 evaluation identities, and prompt construction remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The SAA/IMR and DFM/LDC ablations, activation analysis, parameter sensitivity study, and supplementary applications are retained. V1 Figure 11 becomes v2 Figure 12; the new SAA process diagram adds explanation rather than another analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The existing seed-related illustration in Figure 1 is also retained.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds OMG-InstantID scores of 0.231/0.657/0.343/0.742 and StoryMaker scores of 0.219/0.678/0.147/0.296, ordered as CLIP-T/FaceSim/Expr/Pose. All pre-existing table scores remain unchanged. Multi-ID qualitative examples are revised, while the single-ID comparison decreases from six example rows to three.

T1.justification: V2 adds the explicit condition beta > 1 alongside Equation 3, providing a limited clarification of the parameter domain. Equations 1–8 otherwise remain unchanged, with no new theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the claim that IMR leverages contrastive learning with feature-space manipulation, aligning its characterization with the retained method. The principal claims about zero-shot multi-ID generation, facial editing, task-decoupled training, and VariFace-10k remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 newly identifies difficulty generating faces near image edges in Section 5; the earlier complex-prompt limitation remains. It also extends the facial-replication interpretation to the added baselines, but incorrectly describes OMG-InstantID as having higher FaceSim than DynamicID: Table 2 gives 0.657 versus 0.664.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address. Appendix Section 7.2 and Figure 11 provide additional SAA implementation guidance, including timestep-dependent guidance and suppression of other identities' regions. Existing training and dataset-construction details are retained.

R1.justification: OMG and StoryMaker are added to the references and multi-ID discussion, including a description of StoryMaker's cross-attention loss and ControlNet use. Previously listed OneActor and SpotActor references gain in-text citations. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract, condenses the conclusion, and makes localized prose and terminology edits. It adds a main-text limitations section while retaining the appendix limitations, introduces an SAA appendix subsection, and adds an equal-contribution note. Most text and the overall section sequence are preserved.

P2.justification: The multi-ID comparison moves from v1 Figure 2 to an expanded v2 Figure 6, and the single-ID figure loses three rows. V2 adds the detailed SAA diagram, updates training-diagram loss labels, expands Table 2, and relocates Table 5. Most other figures and the document's visual format remain intact.

improvement.justification: The additional multi-ID baselines modestly strengthen comparative evidence, while the SAA diagram, code pointer, corrected abstract characterization, and specific edge-face limitation improve clarity and documentation. These gains outweigh the reduced single-ID visual examples and localized FaceSim interpretation error in Section 4.2. The unchanged core method and existing results make the overall improvement limited.
